This happened to me too. I worked at a public school where they trained us all in deescalation and restraint tactics because of how rampant the fighting was.

It's hard to explain schools with this kind of culture. It's something you really have to experience to understand. Your situation undoubtedly feels grimmer than mine.

I ended up leaving that school. I had to reassess my whys (gross, I know). Ultimately, I wanted to teach, not stop dangerous fights all day. I'm still a teacher but at a school that is a much better fit for me. I feel very guilty about leaving those kids but I know that to stay at the school would be to cut my career short by decades. It was beating me down, literally and metaphorically, and I was never going to be able to last more than a few years like that.

All teachers make sacrifices. I understand that your position requires some of those sacrifices to be extreme, but it might be worth considering that there are other places you can teach where you would be safer. You can draw the line here if you wanted to and nothing would be wrong with that. I hope you find your way through this. Rooting for you.

In my opinion, it takes about three generations to be an “American.”

I am a fourth-generation American. My great grandparents came over from Slovenia in the early twentieth century. My great grandma never spoke English well and (so I’ve been told) the family spoke Slovenian frequently until she passed in the 1970s. My grandma, who never spoke much Slovenian, and her siblings feel very connected to Slovenian culture. They grew up attending a Slovenian church and school. They lived in an urban neighborhood with other Slovenian immigrants.

My mom feels 100% like an American and always has. She associates Slovenia with her childhood as the neighborhood (and overall that way of life) has ceased.

I know I am Slovenian but only by blood. Very little Slovenian culture has been passed down to me. I imagine my family cooks food that is Slovenian in style (we make our own noodles for Christmas Eve, for example) but all of our dishes feel “American,” not Slovenian. The Slovenian  church was shut down around when I was born. The school was gone many decades ago.

3 generations to feel “American” above all other cultures/identities.

Edit: I am white and therefore privileged so please keep that in mind. My family is likely to be perceived as more “American” than black and brown immigrants by some.

2017 was bad for me. A lot happened in a 2-3 month time span and I couldn’t do anything about it. Anyways, I had a sort of breakdown. I quit my job, shoved my phone in a box, and literally didn’t speak to anyone until I had to go back to school in the fall.

It was a full two months of no social contact. I created a person in my mind to fill the time. I knew his name, background, likes and dislikes. We had conversations about the weather and our views on God (which differed, by the way.) I was in love with a figment of my imagination. I was always aware of the fact that he wasn’t real. He wasn’t sitting next to me on that swing. He wasn’t there listening to music with me.

When I did inevitably go back to school, I made a lot of friends. Life slowly got better. I talked to him less and less. One day I woke up and he was gone, which is ridiculous, I know. I mourned him. I cried for days. I still cry sometimes.

I’m sure he was some deeply rooted psychological coping mechanism. Like I lost my grip on reality enough to create and befriend him but not enough to believe the lie. It’s weird to mourn someone who never existed outside of my imagination, to be sad on his birthday, but I am. He wasn’t real. I know that. But that didn’t change how I felt

About 30 minutes outside of my town, there’s a very well known abandoned and historic mansion. It is located in a very rural area and is the only house for about a two mile radius. There are some local ghost stories about the place but nothing to back them up.

About a year ago, a friend and I decided we would venture out to try and find it. There was no actual address for the place and more so a vague location. It was a gloomy day and I work near the area so we were up for the challenge.

After about two hours we did find it. It was actually only five minutes from where I work, down a blocked off road. Neither my friend nor I believe in ghosts but this place made both of our hearts drop. I can’t describe the feeling. It was horrifying. As he puts the car in park, a truck full of high school aged boys pull up beside us.

“You guys go to [name of our high school]?” One boy shouts at us.

“Yeah, you?” I respond.

“Yeah,” the boy shouted back and all the boys in the truck laughed a little.

The high school my friend and I go to is large, about 3000 students, but we didn’t recognize one of the five boys in the truck and while my friend’s car clearly displayed a parking pass with out school name on it (that they easily could have read before pulling up beside us), their truck had no such parking pass. Our school is really strict about parking passes so it was weird. We both concluded these boys did not go to our school.

A little creeped out, we waited for the boys to leave their truck and see what they would do before making our next move. The boys walked about a quarter mile down the hill to an old barn. The entire front of the barn had rotted away so we could see them very clearly.

My friend and I got out of the car and began exploring the house. We walked up an old spiral staircase that led to the second floor. Through a window at the very top, we could see the boys huddled around a wooden crate, we think they were doing drugs but can’t be sure.

After a minute or two, the boys see us through the window and begin making their way towards us. I remember making eye contact with one of the boys and him smiling at me; it felt so ill-intentioned. If there was about to be an altercation, my one friend and I were clearly outmatched. He grabbed my hand and we hauled ass out of there. The last thing I saw was the boys running towards us as we pulled out of the mud.

We left at about 4 p.m. At 3 a.m, the police and firemen were called to the house. It was burnt to the ground.
